description: Hand-written calibration pairs for duplicate detection (fix_issue.duplicates.find_similar_issues). Four made-up projects; none of the text comes from the benchmark. Each pair is (new issue, recently resolved candidate) labelled 'duplicate' (same root cause) or 'distinct' (hard negative: same module, same keywords, same symptom or error type, or a feature request next to a bug). Within a project the resolved issues are distinct bugs and every new issue duplicates at most one of them, so issue x candidate combinations not listed are distinct too.

inkwell.about: static site generator (markdown -> HTML, front matter, sitemap, RSS)

resolved.title: Front matter dates are parsed as UTC, so posts show up one day early
resolved.body:
Posts with `date: 2024-03-10` in their front matter are listed as March 9 on the index and in the
post header for sites configured with `timezone = "America/New_York"`. The front matter parser built a
naive midnight datetime and then converted it as if it were UTC. Fixed in `inkwell/frontmatter.py` by
localising the date to the site timezone before formatting.

resolved.title: sitemap.xml includes draft pages
resolved.body:
Pages marked `draft: true` were excluded from the generated index pages but were still written to
sitemap.xml, so search engines crawled and indexed them. `build_sitemap()` now skips drafts, same as
the index builder.

resolved.title: Fenced code blocks inside list items lose their indentation
resolved.body:
A fenced code block nested in a bulleted list item is rendered with all leading whitespace removed,
which breaks Python examples. The renderer dedented list-item content once for the list and once more
for the code fence. Fixed in `renderer.py` (dedent only once).

resolved.title: RSS feed item links are relative instead of absolute
resolved.body:
`<link>` entries in feed.xml are `/posts/foo/` instead of `https://example.com/posts/foo/`, so feed
readers cannot open them. Feed URLs are now joined with `base_url`.

issues.title: Every blog post shows yesterday's date
issues.body:
I published a post today with `date: 2024-11-02` at the top of the markdown file, but the homepage
and the post page both say November 1, 2024. Same for all my older posts, they are all one day behind.
My inkwell.toml has `timezone = "America/Los_Angeles"`. Running inkwell 0.9.1 on macOS.

issues.title: Front matter date with a time raises ValueError
issues.body:
Using `date: 2024-03-10 14:30` in front matter makes the build fail with
`ValueError: Invalid isoformat string: '2024-03-10 14:30'`. Only plain dates (2024-03-10) work.
Expected: a date with hours and minutes (no seconds) is accepted.

issues.title: Unfinished posts are showing up in Google
issues.body:
I keep work-in-progress posts in the repo with `draft: true`. They are not on my blog, which is
correct, but Google has indexed them anyway. Looking at the build output, the URLs of those drafts are
listed in /sitemap.xml.

issues.title: Feature request: exclude individual pages from the sitemap
issues.body:
I'd like a front matter flag such as `sitemap: false` to leave published pages like /thanks/ or
/404/ out of sitemap.xml. They should still be built and reachable, just not advertised to crawlers.

issues.title: Copied code examples fail with IndentationError
issues.body:
In my docs I have a numbered list of steps, and step 2 contains a fenced python block:

    1. Install
    2. Add a hook:
       ```python
       def on_build(site):
           return site
       ```

On the rendered page the `return` line is no longer indented, so anyone who copies the snippet gets
`IndentationError: expected an indented block after function definition on line 1`. Outside of a
list the same block renders fine.

issues.title: No syntax highlighting for toml code blocks
issues.body:
Fenced code blocks tagged ```toml render as plain monospace text, while python, js and bash blocks
are highlighted. Looks like the highlighter's language map has no entry for toml.

issues.title: feed.xml has relative URLs
issues.body:
Feedly reports every post link in my feed as broken. feed.xml contains `<link>/posts/hello-world/</link>`
with no domain in front.

issues.title: RSS feed only contains the 10 newest posts
issues.body:
feed.xml is capped at 10 items. Is there a setting for the limit? I'd like the whole archive to be
available to feed readers, or at least a configurable number like `feed_items = 50`.

harbor.about: HTTP client library (retries, redirects, cookies, decoding)

resolved.title: Retries are not applied to connection timeouts
resolved.body:
`Client(retries=3)` retries 502/503 responses, but a `ConnectTimeout` is raised immediately on the
first attempt. The retry loop in `harbor/retry.py` only caught `HTTPStatusError`. It now also retries
`ConnectTimeout` and `ConnectError` (the request was never sent, so this is safe for every method).

resolved.title: Authorization header is forwarded on cross-domain redirects
resolved.body:
When a request to api.example.com is redirected to a different host, the `Authorization` header was
copied onto the redirected request. The header is now stripped whenever a redirect changes the host or
downgrades the scheme.

resolved.title: Cookies set with a Path attribute are sent to every path
resolved.body:
A cookie set with `Set-Cookie: session=abc; Path=/admin` was attached to requests for `/public` as
well. The cookie jar ignored the path attribute when selecting cookies for a request. Path matching per
RFC 6265 section 5.1.4 is now applied.

resolved.title: Response.json() fails when the body starts with a UTF-8 BOM
resolved.body:
Some APIs prefix their JSON with a byte order mark, and `Response.json()` raised
`JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM`. JSON bodies are now decoded with `utf-8-sig`.

issues.title: ConnectTimeout raised even though retries=5
issues.body:
Our VPN drops the first connection attempt pretty often, so I configured `Client(retries=5)` and
expected it to try again. It gives up on the very first timeout:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sync.py", line 41, in <module>
    resp = client.get(url)
  File ".../harbor/client.py", line 212, in get
    return self._send(req)
  File ".../harbor/retry.py", line 58, in send_with_retries
    return transport.send(request)
harbor.exceptions.ConnectTimeout: timed out after 5.0s connecting to 10.0.3.7:443
```

harbor 2.3.0, Python 3.12.

issues.title: POST requests are re-sent after a read timeout
issues.body:
With `retries=3`, a POST that times out while waiting for the response body is sent again. Our
payment provider then received the same order twice. Requests that may already have reached the server
(read timeouts) should not be retried for non-idempotent methods like POST and PATCH.

issues.title: Bearer token sent to a third-party host after a 302
issues.body:
Our API answers download requests with a 302 to an S3 presigned URL. S3 then fails with
`400 InvalidArgument: Only one auth mechanism allowed` because harbor sends our
`Authorization: Bearer ...` header along to the S3 host. Downloading the presigned URL directly works.

issues.title: 307 redirect is not followed for POST
issues.body:
A POST answered with `307 Temporary Redirect` is returned to the caller as-is instead of being re-sent
to the Location with the same method and body. 301 and 302 are followed. `follow_redirects=True` is set.

issues.title: JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig)
issues.body:
Calling `.json()` on responses from our ERP's REST endpoint fails with

    json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)

`json.loads(resp.content.decode("utf-8-sig"))` works, so the payload itself is valid.

issues.title: Response.text falls back to ISO-8859-1 for JSON without a charset
issues.body:
For `Content-Type: application/json` without a `charset` parameter, `resp.text` is decoded as
latin-1, so `ü` comes out as `Ã¼`. JSON is UTF-8 by definition (RFC 8259), so that should be the
default for JSON responses.

issues.title: Feature request: persist cookies to disk
issues.body:
It would be useful to have `CookieJar.save(path)` and `CookieJar.load(path)` so that a logged-in
session survives a restart of our CLI tool instead of having to log in every time.

issues.title: Retries are not applied to 429 responses
issues.body:
When the server answers `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header, harbor returns the
response straight away even with `retries=3`. Status-based retries only cover 502, 503 and 504.
429 should be retried after waiting for the Retry-After delay.

issues.title: Admin session cookie leaks to public pages
issues.body:
After logging into /admin, our session cookie (it is set with `Path=/admin`) is also attached to every
request harbor makes for /static/... and /api/public/..., which we can see in our CDN logs. It should
only be sent to /admin URLs.

resolved.title: Thumbnails of portrait phone photos are rotated 90 degrees
resolved.body:
JPEGs taken on phones store their orientation in the EXIF Orientation tag (usually 6 or 8).
`make_thumbnail()` ignored the tag, so portrait photos came out sideways. Fixed by applying
`ImageOps.exif_transpose()` before resizing.

resolved.title: Transparent PNGs get a black background in JPEG thumbnails
resolved.body:
Converting RGBA PNGs to JPEG thumbnails filled the transparent pixels with black. The image is now
composited onto a white background first (configurable with `background=`).

resolved.title: Worker memory grows without bound on large batches
resolved.body:
The worker kept every opened `Image` in a module-level cache dict that was never evicted, so
processing 10k images used about 6 GB of RAM. The cache is now an LRU bounded to 64 entries and images
are closed after the thumbnail is written.

issues.title: Uploaded profile pictures appear sideways
issues.body:
When users upload a selfie from an iPhone, the avatar preview is turned on its side. The original file
looks fine in the photo viewer and on the phone. Pictures uploaded from desktop computers are fine.

issues.title: Thumbnails are stretched instead of keeping the aspect ratio
issues.body:
`make_thumbnail(img, (200, 200))` on a 1600x900 photo returns a 200x200 image and the picture is
squashed. Expected 200x113, i.e. fit inside the box and keep the proportions.

issues.title: Logo thumbnails have black boxes around them
issues.body:
Our partner logos are PNG files with a transparent background. In the generated .jpg thumbnails the
transparent area is solid black, which looks terrible on our white product pages.

issues.title: Feature request: WebP thumbnails with transparency
issues.body:
Please support `format="webp"` for thumbnails. WebP supports an alpha channel, so logos and cut-out
product shots could keep their transparency instead of being flattened into a JPEG.

issues.title: pixelpress worker gets OOM-killed during the nightly batch
issues.body:
Our nightly job that creates thumbnails for ~20,000 product images is killed by the kernel OOM killer
after about an hour. Watching the process, RSS climbs steadily with every image and never goes down.
Restarting the worker every 2,000 images works around it.

issues.title: Huge TIFF scans make the worker run out of memory
issues.body:
A single 30000x20000 px TIFF (a scanned map) makes the worker allocate more than 8 GB and crash
immediately. Very large images should be decoded at reduced size (draft/reduce) or rejected above a
configurable pixel limit.

resolved.title: Sync conflict silently overwrites the newer version of a note
resolved.body:
When the same note was edited on two devices while offline, whichever device synced last won, even if
its edit was older. The merge step now compares `updatedAt` and, when both sides changed, keeps both
versions and creates a "conflicted copy" note.

resolved.title: Search does not match accented words
resolved.body:
Searching for `cafe` did not find notes containing `café`, and the other way round. The search index
now stores NFKD-normalised tokens with diacritics removed, and queries are normalised the same way.

resolved.title: Crash when opening a note whose attachment upload failed
resolved.body:
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'mimeType')` in `AttachmentView.render` when
a failed upload left an attachment record without a file. Such records are now rendered as a "missing
attachment" placeholder.

issues.title: Lost an hour of edits after my laptop came back online
issues.body:
I edited a meeting note on my laptop on the train with no internet. My phone still had the old version
of that note open. When the laptop reconnected, my changes vanished and the note showed the phone's
older text. Nothing in the trash either.

issues.title: Sync stuck at "Uploading 1 of 3" forever
issues.body:
The sync spinner never finishes when one of the changed notes has a 40 MB video attachment. The other
two notes are never uploaded either. Removing the attachment lets sync complete.

issues.title: Searching 'resume' doesn't find 'résumé'
issues.body:
I have a note titled "Résumé tips". Typing resume in the search box returns nothing; typing résumé
(with the accents) finds it. On my phone keyboard typing accents is a pain.

issues.title: Search doesn't match words with accents
issues.body:
My note "Naïve Bayes notes" can't be found by searching naive. It only shows up when I type the ï.
Version 3.2 on Android.

issues.title: Tag search is case-sensitive
issues.body:
Searching for `#Work` finds my tagged notes but `#work` finds none. Tags should match regardless of
upper/lower case.

issues.title: Blank screen with TypeError reading 'mimeType'
issues.body:
Opening one particular note shows a blank screen. The console says:

    TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'mimeType')
        at AttachmentView.render (attachment-view.js:88:31)
        at renderNote (note.js:144:12)

That note had an image whose upload failed yesterday when my connection dropped.

issues.title: TypeError reading 'title' after deleting a notebook
issues.body:
Deleting a notebook that still contains notes shows

    TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'title')
        at NotebookList.render (notebook-list.js:51:20)

The sidebar still holds a reference to the deleted notebook. Reloading the app fixes it.
